subject: Dedicated capacity: isolation constraints, scaling expectations & SLA decision path
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Connor Ellis <connor.ellis@nebulaai.com>, Priya Shah <priya@nebulaai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: isolation constraints, scaling expectations & SLA decision path

Hi Connor / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the level of detail on NebulaAI's production requirements. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the implications for a dedicated (reserved GPU) deployment, and proposed next steps.

Key pain points (your language):
- Multi-tenant risk: customer-facing inference must be logically isolated from internal dev models and partner integrations.
- Predictable tail latency: p95 SLO target of <=250ms for short/contextual generation (<=512 tokens).
- Cost predictability at scale: you want a committed baseline but the ability to burst for peaks.
- Compliance: audit logs and data separation for regulated verticals are required.

Summary of what we propose (high-level):
- Deployment: dedicated GPU pool (single-tenant reservation) in our us-west region with tenant-level namespace isolation.
- Sizing guidance: initial reserved pool = 4xA100-equivalent GPUs for baseline throughput; burst capacity via autoscale to 8 GPUs for peak windows (billing on burst).
- Runtime: KV cache reuse per-tenant + prefix caching to preserve latency while reducing token compute.
- SLA: baseline availability SLA 99.9% for the dedicated pool; per-request latency SLO monitoring and escalation runbooks (we'll share a draft SLA).
- Security/compliance: KMS integration for model keys, audit log retention (90 days standard, extended options available).

Immediate asks we need from you to finalize commercial & ops terms:
1) Rough steady-state qps and 95th/99th percentile token-per-request distribution (you shared peaks but a sample baseline will help).
2) Any hard compliance constraints (HIPAA, SOC2 timeline, or customer-specific audit windows).
3) A procurement contact and cadence for contract review (PM/Legal).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- I’ll share an initial reserved-plan workbook and SLA draft (attached).
- Schedule a 45-min technical sizing review with Ben (our SE) to validate peak shaping and isolation approach — proposed window: this Thu or Fri.
- Onboarding plan: 6–8 week onboarding (provisioning, canary traffic, monitoring hooks), faster if you provide a short dev dataset and test tokens earlier.

Attachments: nebula-dedicated-reserved-plan-v1.xlsx (workbook with baseline / burst cost scenarios), SLA-draft-redwood-nebula.pdf (draft ed. 0.1).

If this matches your understanding I’ll move to lock an SE slot and get a procurement packet over to Priya.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Connor Ellis <connor.ellis@nebulaai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@nebulaai.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:40:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: isolation constraints, scaling expectations & SLA decision path

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few details and adding context so we can size correctly.

Confirmed pain & context:
- Isolation: must ensure our partner models and internal research models cannot access live customer KV caches or logs. Logical isolation is fine; we may require a dedicated tenant layer for 3rd party partner integrations.
- Latency: our median is ~80ms today; p95 spikes up to 420ms during peak. Goal is to get p95 <=250ms for 95% of requests within 60 days of launch.
- Traffic profile: baseline 120 qps (short prompts ~60 tokens), daily peaks up to 520 qps for short windows (15–30m).
- Tokens/month: ~2.4B currently, projected to 4.5B in 6 months.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress; need audit logs and evidence of key rotation procedures.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood support strict logical isolation for partner integrations as a paid add-on? If yes, is there an architecture doc we can share with infosec?
2) Regarding burst: how is burst billed vs reserved capacity? Do you offer a blended monthly commit option?
3) Do you have a standard canary and rollback window (we'd like to limit initial canaries to non-customer traffic for one week).

Priya will be our procurement lead — she'll take the packet and coordinate legal. We'll confirm tech slots by EOD.

Connor
VP Product, NebulaAI
connor.ellis@nebulaai.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Connor Ellis <connor.ellis@nebulaai.com>, Priya Shah <priya@nebulaai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: isolation constraints, scaling expectations & SLA decision path

Connor / Priya — great, thanks for the additional traffic and compliance detail. Short answers to your questions and next logistical items below.

1) Partner isolation model: yes — we offer a "partner namespace" option that creates strict logical boundaries (separate KV caches, ACLs, and optional dedicated model replicas). I'll attach a short architecture note in the SE review. This is an add-on (one-time config + modest monthly premium).

2) Burst billing / commit options: two common approaches:
  - Reserved baseline + pay-as-you-go burst: reserve X GPUs for month-on-month discount; burst to additional GPUs billed at on-demand token/GPU rates.
  - Blended commit: a larger monthly commit that covers expected burst windows at a lower blended rate. The attached workbook has a comparison; we can model both for your 4.5B token projection.

3) Canary windows: standard canary process is 72 hours for restricted traffic + 5 business days of expanded non-customer traffic. We can accommodate your one-week non-customer-only canary; we'll note that in the onboarding runbook.

Proposed logistics and owners:
- SE sizing session (Ben): Thu 16 Jul 2026, 11:00–11:45 PT — agenda: traffic shaping, cache strategy, replica counts for p95 goals. Ben, can you take this?
- Procurement packet -> Priya: I'll send a commercial term sheet + initial SOW by EOD Wed.
- Compliance artifacts: Monica will prepare SOC2 in-progress notes and KMS rotation evidence (Monica: target to have package in 5 business days).

Ben: quick ask for the SE session — please include an ops canary checklist and an estimation of warm-up time for KV caches at the targeted traffic ramp.

Connor / Priya: if that schedule works I’ll calendar the SE slot and share the workbook with cost scenarios across the two billing approaches.

Best,
Aditya

--
Aditya Rao

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: SE prep notes for NebulaAI sizing session (Thu)

Internal note (do not forward externally):

Quick technical checklist I put together for the SE call — keeping it short so we can run through on Thu:
- Confirm baseline model family and weights (Connor mentioned Llama-derivative; need explicit topology + quantization targets).
- Replica math: for 120 qps baseline with 60-token avg and p95 target <=250ms, estimate 4 A100-equivalents reserved, burst to 8 for the 520 qps peaks (see worksheet).
- KV cache warm-up: recommend pre-warmed cache step during canary with synthetic prefixes; warm-up latency expected ~10–30s per active tenant depending on sequence reuse.
- Isolation config: partner-namespace requires dedicated replica group or strict tenant-scoped ACLs + separate logging sinks — flagged as add-on in quote.
- Monitoring hooks: provide request-level tracing (x-request-id), per-tenant cost tagging, and p95 alerting at +40% of baseline.
- Ops playbook: rollback plan (instant revert to hosted fallback), traffic-shifting script, and runbook entry for capacity failover to another region (if cross-region failover needed).

I'll bring these slides and the replica math to the call. Aditya, Monica — suggest we have a 15-min pre-call at 10:30 Thu to align on answers and who will own each action.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
